# Pre-print checklist

46 items across 8 phases. Run the whole list before the files go to the printer. Report results phase by phase, quoting the failing line of the rulebook for each miss.

## 1. Content completeness

- [ ] Every component in the box appears in the illustrated component list, with the correct count
      - *Why:* Count errors are the most common shipped defect (Obsession)
- [ ] Every rule printed on a card, board, mat or player aid also exists in the rulebook
      - *Why:* Rules that live only on a component vanish when the component does (Mage Knight, Triplock)
- [ ] Setup is fully specified for every supported player count
      - *Why:* Player-count deltas are the most re-looked-up fact in most games
- [ ] Tie-breakers exist for every 'the most / the least / first place' rule
      - *Why:* Superlatives are the classic hole-generator
- [ ] Solo / cooperative / variant modes have their own complete setup and end conditions
      - *Why:* Imperium shipped with a missing solo-bot rule
- [ ] End-game trigger AND end-of-game sequence are both stated (does the round finish?)
      - *Why:* 'Finish the round' is assumed far more often than it is written

## 2. Structure

- [ ] Goal / win condition appears before the detailed rules
      - *Why:* Readers need a purpose to attach rules to
- [ ] No term is used before it is defined
      - *Why:* The single most-cited reader irritation
- [ ] Every forward reference cites its target section and page
      - *Why:* Uncited forward references force blind page-flipping
- [ ] Exceptions and edge cases sit beside their rule or in a clearly marked section, not inline in the core flow
      - *Why:* Exceptions in the main flow make the core unlearnable
- [ ] Each rule sits under the heading a confused player would actually reach for
      - *Why:* Organisation is a retrieval problem, not only a teaching one
- [ ] One linear read is sufficient to understand the game
      - *Why:* Ryan Migalla's quality metric

## 3. Language

- [ ] One concept = one term, everywhere, including cards and marketing copy
      - *Why:* Synonyms force readers to hunt for a difference that does not exist
- [ ] Effects that behave identically are worded identically (templating)
      - *Why:* Consistent templating lets players learn a pattern once
- [ ] Conditions precede effects in every conditional rule
      - *Why:* Reduces misplays and enables skimming
- [ ] No sentence fails the one-breath test
      - *Why:* Long sentences are the main source of parse failure
- [ ] 'should' removed; 'exception' and 'remember' reviewed as design smells
      - *Why:* Stonemaier's editorial pass
- [ ] Repeated sets always listed in the same canonical order
      - *Why:* Silent, cumulative cognitive load

## 4. Examples & visuals

- [ ] Every example covers at least one non-obvious case
      - *Why:* Obvious examples are wasted print
- [ ] No rule appears only inside an example, caption or parenthetical
      - *Why:* Paul Grogan's red flag
- [ ] Examples make clear which details are arbitrary
      - *Why:* Readers infer unintended rules from examples
- [ ] There is a labelled setup diagram of the initial table state
      - *Why:* Lets readers verify their setup visually
- [ ] Information-dense components have an anatomy diagram
      - *Why:* Converts a component into shared vocabulary

## 5. Reference apparatus

- [ ] Table of contents present (and an index if the book exceeds ~12 pages)
      - *Why:* TOC and index are different tools
- [ ] Icon key exists in exactly one place and is easy to find
      - *Why:* Icon soup without a key is a top complaint
- [ ] Back cover carries turn flow, icon key and/or setup summary
      - *Why:* The most valuable page in the book
- [ ] A short 'commonly missed rules' list exists
      - *Why:* Highest value per word available
- [ ] Rulebook carries a version number and date
      - *Why:* Enables errata and living rules

## 6. Typography & print

- [ ] Body text >= 10pt (12pt preferred); test the smallest text in dim light
      - *Why:* 10pt is the stated floor at Stonemaier; accessibility guidance says 12pt
- [ ] Contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text; page still readable in greyscale
      - *Why:* WCAG-derived target
- [ ] No rules text over art, texture or dark backgrounds
      - *Why:* Recurring cause of games being shelved
- [ ] No colour-only coding anywhere; every distinction is double-coded
      - *Why:* 8% of men have colour vision deficiency
- [ ] No underlined rules text; all-caps limited to a handful of critical notes
      - *Why:* Legibility
- [ ] Short sections do not break across pages; 2-page sections are on facing pages
      - *Why:* Prevents mid-rule page turns
- [ ] Page count divisible by 4; spreads planned deliberately
      - *Why:* Print reality

## 7. Testing

- [ ] At least one full blind playtest with people who have never seen the game
      - *Why:* The only reliable detector of missing rules
- [ ] At least one blind test with non-gamers or non-native speakers
      - *Why:* Experienced gamers paper over defects
- [ ] Testers were told not to use how-to-play videos
      - *Why:* Not every owner will have internet access
- [ ] Designer did not intervene except to protect the rest of the test
      - *Why:* Intervention destroys the data
- [ ] Timed look-up test on the pre-production copy: can a specific answer be found fast?
      - *Why:* Slow look-up is a structural defect
- [ ] Rulebook read backwards, section by section, as a final QA pass
      - *Why:* Prevents autopilot skimming

## 8. Handover

- [ ] A written style guide accompanies the text to the copyeditor and proofreader
      - *Why:* Cheapest possible consistency insurance
- [ ] Editing done before layout; proofreading done after layout
      - *Why:* Layout introduces its own errors
- [ ] Instructions to the graphic designer are unmistakably not rules text
      - *Why:* Bracketed notes have shipped as rules before
- [ ] Rulebook version matches the component version being printed
      - *Why:* Version drift is a classic defect source
- [ ] Searchable PDF and a public living-rules/errata page are planned
      - *Why:* Ctrl-F is the index every game already ships with
